# Baruch Chapter 5 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Vaticanus, Baruch 5

---

**1** Take off, O Jerusalem, the garment of your mourning and affliction, and put on forever the beauty of the glory from God.

**2** Clothe yourself in the double cloak of the righteousness that comes from God; and set on your head the diadem of the glory of the Eternal.

**3** For God will show your splendor to every nation under heaven.

**4** For your name will be called by God forever: Peace of Righteousness and Glory of Godliness.

**5** Arise, O Jerusalem, and stand on the height, and look toward the east, and see your children gathered from the rising of the sun to its setting, at the word of the Holy One, rejoicing that God has remembered them.

**6** For they went out from you on foot, led away by enemies; but God is bringing them back to you, borne in glory as on a royal throne.

**7** For God has commanded that every high mountain and the everlasting hills be made low, and the valleys filled up, to level the ground, so that Israel may walk safely in the glory of God.

**8** The woods and every fragrant tree have overshadowed Israel at God's command.

**9** For God will lead Israel with joy, in the light of his glory, with the mercy and righteousness that come from him.

---

## Council Notes

**On v.1 — position of "forever":** EMET places "forever" with the garment of mourning ("put on the beauty of the glory from God forever"); LOGOS and PNEUMA attach it to the beauty/glory: "put on forever the beauty of the glory from God." The Greek eis ton aiōna modifies the putting-on. Consensus follows LOGOS placement: "put on forever."

**On v.2 — "double cloak" vs. "double garment" vs. "diadem":** EMET "double garment"; LOGOS "double cloak"; PNEUMA "double cloak." The Greek diploidia = a doubled/folded garment, a robe of honor. "Cloak" is slightly more specific and evocative. Consensus: "double cloak."

**On v.4 — the divine name:** The formal declaration "your name will be called..." is a renaming formula. All agents capitalize "Peace of Righteousness" and "Glory of Godliness" as a formal name. PNEUMA adds "new name" (not in the Greek) but the concept is correct. Consensus: without "new."

**On v.6 — "as if on a royal throne" vs. "as on a royal throne":** EMET "as on a royal throne"; LOGOS "as if on a royal throne." Greek hōs epi thronou basilikēs = as on a royal throne. No "as if" — the comparison is direct. Consensus: "as on a royal throne."

**On v.7 — Isaiah 40 echo:** All agents note this clearly. The correspondence is close enough to suggest deliberate literary dependence. The consensus text preserves the echo exactly without editorial annotation. Readers familiar with Isa 40:4 and Luke 3:5 will recognize it.

**On v.8 — "overshadowed" vs. "shaded":** EMET "overshadowed"; LOGOS "shaded"; PNEUMA "spread their shade." Greek eskiasen = gave shade / overshadowed. "Overshadowed" has a slightly more majestic quality (cf. Luke 1:35, 9:34 where the same verb describes the divine cloud). The choice is between naturalness and resonance. Consensus: "overshadowed" for its richer connotative range.

**On v.9 — structure of the final verse:** The verse ends with three parallel gifts: joy, the light of his glory, mercy and righteousness. All agents preserve the tripartite structure. The final line is the theological summation of the whole book: God leading his people with joy, in light, with mercy and righteousness.
